name: Skulk
body:
Skulks are a secretive people who live hidden in and under many settlements.

While they especially like to congregate where humans are present, skulks can be found hidden in the shadows of many worlds. While they are by nature anti-social, they are also very crafty.

Physical

Skulks are roughly the same size as a human, though they are significantly more gaunt and gangly-looking. Female and male skulks look nearly identical. They usually wear little or no clothing, leaving as much of their skin exposed as possible. Their skin is naturally a dull gray color, but like a chameleon a skulk has incredible control over its color. They can easily camouflage themselves to blend in with natural features such as leaves, dirt, or stone—or even brightly-colored features such as flowers or murals. While they cannot quickly duplicate the fine detail of their background, with practice a skulk can create complex patterns on their own skin like tattoos. They can also choose to disguise their skin in various humanoid flesh tones, or even make their skin stand out by making it a bright, unusual color.

A skulk’s eyes are a pale blue color and pupil-less, and these never change color.

Social

Skulks can be found in many places where other humanoids are found, almost always lurking at the edges of civilization. They are popular among elements of the criminal underworld due to their superior abilities to remain hidden and undetected—and this has caused them to gain a reputation as thieves and thugs.

It is a reputation that is not entirely unearned, as skulk culture emphasizes survival at all cost and places little value on lives outside of one’s own clan. Many skulks therefore develop a cavalier attitude toward murder, theft, and other crimes that they deem necessary for their own way of life. In the harsh reality of the sewers and streets that most skulks call home, the only way of life they learn are violence and resentment.

Nevertheless, few skulks resort to direct confrontation. Stealth and subterfuge are their strengths, and they use these to great effect. Among skulks, there is no dishonor in hiding or fleeing, as this is seen as a cunning short-term tactic to achieve one’s long-term goals.

Skulks prefer subterranean hideouts or wooded areas on the outskirts of town from where they can operate in relative safety and anonymity. They never congregate in large numbers, although small bands may send representatives to barter or negotiate with other skulk clans, criminal organizations, or similar groups that might be of use to them. Anyone who enters into a contract with a skulk clan would be wise to consider that agreement strictly temporary, however.

Alignment And Religion

While there are exceptions, by and large skulks are Chaotic Evil, with most having concern only for their own needs and little patience for rules and conventions.

They typically worship deities devoted to darkness, deception, stealth, and trickery—with some even going so far as to make pacts with gods of blood and murder.

Names

Skulk names are simple and short, using a combination of traditional names passed down among skulks and “street names” earned in the criminal underworld.

Some traditional skulk names include the following (choose or roll 1d12): 1 Hurkaff, 2 Jabbit, 3 Jerrar, 4 Kelma, 5 Luss, 6 Mabbat, 7 Muckram, 8 Mullimar, 9 Neash, 10 Pella, 11 Skalmu, 12 Tabirra

Some examples of skulk “street names” names include (choose or roll 1d12): 1 Blue Eyes, 2 Butterfingers, 3 Creepy Jack, 4 Cuts, 5 Gray, 6 Ha-Ha, 7 Lucky, 8 Shanks, 9 Snake, 10 Socks, 11 Spots, 12 Zero

Standard Species Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You have sharp sense and sharp reflexes, but you have trouble dealing with people directly. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Dex, +2 Wis, –2 Cha [standard]. (0)
Size As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type You are a Humanoid with the skulk subtype. (0)
Speed Your base speed is 30 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking Common. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Dwarven, Elven, Gnome, Goblin, Halfling, and Orc. (0)
Alternate Species Traits
Camouflaged Step You can pass through forest and subterranean settings almost without a trace. Add +10 to the DC to track you in these environments. (2)
Chameleon Skin You excel at blending into your environment, giving you a +4 species bonus on Stealth checks. Your species bonus comes largely from your ability to change the color of your skin to match your surroundings—even complex or regular patterns like bricks and mortar. This bonus is halved if you are wearing armor, or if you’re wearing or carrying any item that is too difficult to conceal. Wearing normal, light clothing and carrying small items, you can cleverly reveal enough of your skin and hide any carried items behind you so that you gain the benefits of this ability. (4)
Low-light Vision You can see twice as far as a human in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. You retain the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions. (1)
Silent Hunter You reduce the penalty for using Stealth while moving by 5 and can make Stealth checks while running at a –20 penalty (this number includes the penalty reduction from this trait). (2)
Stalker Perception and Stealth are always class skills for you. (1)
Total: 10 RP (standard)
Variants
Psionic Skulk

While rare, some skulks do develop mental powers far beyond those of their common kin.

Naturally Psionic You gain Wild Talent as a bonus feat at 1st level. If you take levels in a psionic class, you instead gain the Psionic Talent feat. This trait replaces camouflaged step.
Psionic Aptitude When you take a level in a favored class, you can choose to gain an additional power point instead of a hit point or skill point. This trait replaces stalker.
Skulk Psionics Once per day, you can use cloud mind as a psi-like ability. The manifester level for this effect is equal to 1/2 your character level (minimum 1), and Wisdom is your manifesting ability. This trait replaces silent hunter.
Alternate Species Traits
Arctic Hunter Add +10 to the DC to track you in snow, ice, and similar environments. This trait replaces camouflaged step.
Forager You are more comfortable in the wilderness than in the city, and are adept at fending for yourself in the wild. You gain a +2 species bonus to Survival checks. This trait replaces silent hunter.
Hard to Read You gain nondetection and undetectable alignment as constant spell-like abilities, with a caster level equal to your character level. This trait replaces silent hunter.
Tunnel Stalker You are not accustomed to emerging from the subterranean tunnels beneath your city—and your vision has become attuned to life in this eternal gloom. You gain darkvision with a range of 60 feet, but you also have the light sensitivity weakness. This trait replaces low-light vision.
Feats
Chameleon Stealth

You can use your natural camouflage ability to hide in plain sight.

Prerequisite(s): Stealth 6 ranks, skulk.

Benefit(s): You may make Stealth checks even when observed so long as you are unarmored, but you take a –10 penalty when doing so.

Alternative Favored Class Bonuses
Alchemist Add +10 minutes to the duration of your mutagens.
Cleric Select one domain power granted at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Wisdom modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that domain power.
Cryptic Add +1/2 to the number of rounds per day that you can use altered defense.
Fighter Choose the dirty trick or steal combat maneuver. Add +1/3 to your CMB when attempting this maneuver (maximum bonus of +4).
Inquisitor Add a +1/2 bonus on Perception checks to see through magical disguises or pinpoint invisible creatures.
Psychic Warrior Choose the reposition or steal combat maneuver. Add +1/3 to your CMB when attempting this maneuver (maximum bonus of +4).
Ranger Add a +1/4 dodge bonus to AC against your favored enemies.
Rogue Add a +1/2 bonus on your sneak attack damage rolls against flat-footed opponents.
Shifter Add +1/4 to the number of minutes you can assume your minor form each day.
Slayer Gain a +1/3 bonus on Diplomacy checks to gather information, and a +1/3 bonus on Survival checks when underground or in a forest environment.
Soulknife Add +1/2 on critical hit confirmation rolls for attacks made with a mindblade formed as a light weapon (maximum bonus of +4). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Vigilante Gain +1/2 on the Disguise bonus provided by seamless guise.
